name: browser-human-step-code
description:
The kind:code half of request_human_step end to end: a person supplies an emailed login code, the RUNNER types it into the page element the agent named, and the code NEVER reaches the model. The agent navigates to the fixture sign-in page, reads it to get the code field's ref, then calls web_request_human_step(kind=code, ref=<that field>). That BLOCKS, publishing a login_human_step card; startAutoApprover answers it WITH the bundle's autoApproveCode (123456) via the InteractionDecisionPayload.ResponseText carrier — the genuine free-text field a real surface's text input would fill, never the closed ActionID. The runner captures the code off its host, types it into the field via the C4 InsertText path (not a model tool call), and returns a STATUS only.

The no-leak is the point (Review Focus 3): the request_human_step tool RESULT is asserted to contain "entered into ref" and NOT "123456"; the follow-up web_read is asserted to show the page advanced to CODE-ACCEPTED-SIGNED-IN (proving the code reached the field for real) while STILL not containing "123456" (the field is blanked, exactly like a filled credential); and agentReplyNotContains pins the code never reaches the delivered reply. approvalPrompts:1 pins that exactly one card was raised — the run answered the code card rather than hanging to the class timeout, which is what a missing free-text carrier would have produced.

Without autoApproveCode the code card would be approved with an EMPTY answer and the runner would have nothing to type, so this bundle is also the regression guard that the replay auto-answer path can supply a typed code at all.
